name: Rubellite
lede: Rubellite is the pink to red variety of tourmaline, a gem name that gives its color to a vivid raspberry-magenta.

sections.title: Pink tourmaline
sections.body:
A jeweler's glossary defines rubellite as pink tourmaline, with the finest found in Siberia and Burma [1]. Another entry calls it a pinkish or reddish form of tourmaline [2].

A California mine opened in 1903 sent most of its rubellite to Chinese dealers; it was the favorite stone of the Dowager Empress Cixi [1]. Victorians used it in acrostic jewelry: a necklace of fire-opal, opal, ruby, emerald, vermeil, essonite and rubellite spelled out the word forever [2][3]. Like the ruby in the same necklace, it was read in the Victorian sentiment trade as a letter, not as a color [2]. The books give no price or grading details for it, only the places and the people who prized it [1][3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch #BC0061 is a saturated crimson-pink [4]. It sits near [[raspberry]], [[magenta]] and [[crimson]] [4]. Real stones vary from pale pink to deep red, so this is one screen approximation [4].

questions.q: Rubellite is a form of which gem?

openers: Rubellite, pink tourmaline, was the Dowager Empress Cixi's favorite stone.
